task: Brief an engineer deciding whether to adopt Orbital Mesh Sync (OMS): current capabilities, limits, and what changed. Synthesize across the design doc, the issue tracker, and the changelog.

nuggets.text: OMS orders writes using a per-device vector clock
the reference transport is QUIC (pluggable transport design)
conflict resolution is last-writer-wins by default with an optional merge hook
a cold-node mode is designed for devices offline more than 30 days
a fallback TCP transport is in progress and not yet released
last-writer-wins drops concurrent edits in a known race, fix targeted for 1.1
v0.9 was the first public release

integration_facts.text: on-prem deployment is not available: the design deferred key management, it is still backlog and blocks the regulated customers, and v1.0 states on-prem is not supported
the minimum device RAM requirement changed from 512 MB in the design to 256 MB in v1.0
the merge hook went from optional and unstable to stable and frozen in v1.0
unbounded vector-clock growth on cold nodes was identified as an issue and addressed by the v1.0 compaction job
cold-node mode ships but is disabled by default pending field testing

answer_key.q: Is on-prem deployment available in v1.0?
answer_key.a: No. The design deferred key management, it is still backlog (blocks three regulated customers), and the v1.0 notes say on-prem is not supported.

answer_key.q: What is the current minimum device RAM and did it change?
answer_key.a: 256 MB as of v1.0, lowered from the 512 MB design target.

answer_key.q: Is the merge hook stable enough to build on?
answer_key.a: Yes as of v1.0 (promoted to stable and frozen); it was optional and unstable earlier.

answer_key.q: Can you rely on cold-node mode out of the box?
answer_key.a: No. It ships but is disabled by default pending field testing.

answer_key.q: Is there a correctness risk with the default conflict resolution?
answer_key.a: Yes. Last-writer-wins drops concurrent edits in a known race, with a fix targeted for 1.1.
